title: Vocabulary: self
keyIdea: Precise words make your inner life easier to understand and talk about. To notice is to spot something by paying attention; to reflect is to think back on what happened and why. A trigger sets off a feeling, and a pattern is something that happens again and again. An assumption is a guess you have not checked. Impact is the effect your actions have on others, and perspective is how things look from one person's side. Put together, these build self-awareness: knowing your own feelings and habits.

kid: Some words help you talk about what goes on inside you. First you notice: you spot a feeling, like hot cheeks or a tight tummy. Then you reflect: you think back on what happened and why.
A trigger is the thing that sets a feeling off. Being hungry can be a trigger for feeling cross. If it happens again and again, that is a pattern. 'I notice a pattern: I get cross when I rush.'
An assumption is a guess you have not checked. 'Ava did not wave' is what you saw. 'Ava is cross with me' is an assumption. You can check it by asking her.
Impact is the effect you have on other people, even when you did not mean it. Perspective is how things look from one side. Knowing all this about yourself is called self-awareness.
adult: This vocabulary sits in PSHE and the IB PYP 'identity' strand. Pupils learn self-awareness, reflect, notice, pattern, trigger, assumption, impact and perspective, and use them about their own behaviour. Precise labels help children step back from a feeling and describe it, which supports self-regulation.

Three slips are common. Children hear 'reflect' as looking in a mirror rather than thinking back. They call one bad day a 'pattern' when a pattern needs repeats. And they mix up the trigger, which comes before a feeling, with the feeling itself.

The assumption versus fact distinction matters most for friendships. 'He did not sit with me' is noticed; 'he hates me' is assumed and can be checked. Likewise, intent and impact are both real: an accident can still hurt, and naming the impact helps repair it.

In the lab your child matches the words to their meanings, finds the trigger that comes before every grumpy morning in Leo's week, sorts noticed thoughts from assumptions, sees one paint spill from three perspectives, and drops choices into a pond to see their impact.

familyTip: At dinner, each share one thing you noticed about your feelings today, and one trigger. Once a week, reflect together: is there a pattern? Model it yourself: 'I notice I get snappy when I am tired.'

visual.caption: Is each sentence something noticed, or an assumption? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: match self-reflection words, find Leo's trigger in his week, sort noticed from assumed, see three perspectives, and test impact.

practice.prompt: What does 'reflect' mean in 'reflect on your day'?
choices: Think back on what happened and why
Look at yourself in a mirror
practice.hint: It is not about mirrors here. It is about your thinking.
practice.explain: To reflect is to think back on what happened and why. A mirror reflects light, but you reflect on your day.

practice.prompt: Ella felt worried before a test on {n} days this month. What is this?
practice.hint: Something that happens again and again has a name.
practice.explain: A pattern. Worry before a test on {n} days is a repeat, so Ella can plan for it.

practice.prompt: 'Jay did not sit with me, so he does not like me.' What is the part after 'so'?
practice.hint: Did you check it, or guess it?
practice.explain: An assumption: a guess about what Jay thinks. You noticed he did not sit with you; you could ask him why.

practice.prompt: Noah gets cross when he has slept less than {n} hours. What is the trigger?
practice.hint: A trigger comes before the feeling and sets it off.
practice.explain: Not enough sleep (less than {n} hours) sets off the cross feeling, so it is the trigger.

choices: Knowing your own feelings and habits
pool.hint: Self means you. Awareness means knowing.
pool.explain: Self-awareness is knowing your own feelings and habits, like 'I go quiet when I am nervous'.

pool.prompt: Sam spilled paint by accident. Tia's picture is ruined. What is the impact on Tia?
choices: She is upset about her picture
pool.hint: Impact is the effect on someone else, not what you meant.
pool.explain: Tia is upset. The impact is real even though it was an accident, so saying sorry still helps.

pool.prompt: 'From my side it felt unfair, but I can see Tom's side too.' Which word fits?
pool.hint: Which word means how things look from one side?
pool.explain: Perspective. Each person sees the same event from their own side.

pool.prompt: Leo was grumpy once after a spelling test. Is that a pattern?
choices: Yes, any bad day is a pattern
pool.hint: A pattern happens again and again.
pool.explain: No. One time is not a pattern. If it kept happening, it would be.

pool.prompt: Mia noticed her cheeks felt hot {n} times today. What is the first step of self-reflection she has done?
pool.hint: Spotting something by paying attention has a name.
pool.explain: She noticed. Spotting hot cheeks {n} times is noticing; thinking about why comes next.

pool.prompt: Ben is grumpy on {n} school days. Every time, he skipped breakfast. What is the trigger?
pool.hint: Look for what came before the feeling every time.
pool.explain: Skipping breakfast came before every one of the {n} grumpy days, so it is the trigger.

pool.prompt: How can you check an assumption?
pool.hint: An assumption has not been checked yet.
pool.explain: Ask the person. Checking turns a guess into something you know.
